deities: Small figurines of Shiva and goddesses of the Hindu pantheon are kept inside the shrine; ancient cannons of the Jaintia kings are also housed on the premises
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (reportedly the temple's biggest gathering - claimed ~50,000 devotees by local reports; single-source figure, verify)

history.period: 13th century per local claims (UNVERIFIED - no inscriptional, documentary, or ASI confirmation found)
history.summary: An ancient Shiva temple near the Nartiang Durga Temple (seq 1932/701) in Nartiang village, West Jaintia Hills. Local tradition claims a 13th-century Jaintia-king foundation, but no source confirms the date - treat as UNVERIFIED; note that dates for the neighbouring Durga temple range from '13th century' in some visitor accounts to the better-sourced 16th-17th century, so all early dating here is uncertain. The temple was renovated 'a few decades ago' per one report. The shrine houses remains of ancient cannons (a 2010 traveller account describes about 10 cannons, some ~3 m long, kept inside). A partisan Hindu-nationalist outlet (Indus Scrolls, 2021) claims the temple has no Shivlinga because devotees' attempts to install one were opposed by the local Christian-majority population - this is a SINGLE-SOURCE, editorialised claim that could not be independently verified, so it is reported here as a claim, not a fact. The same outlet claims ~50,000 devotees visit on Maha Shivaratri - treat the figure as unverified. FLAG ON CSV TOWN: the temple is at Nartiang village, NOT Jowai (the district town, ~25 km away) - the CSV town is wrong. Coordinates used (25.56729, 92.21087) are the Nartiang Durga Temple's (the Shiv temple is within walking distance); they are APPROXIMATE for this temple - verify. No verified photograph of the Shiv temple itself was found after genuine image searching (results showed only the Durga temple and the monoliths), so media is empty - flagged.

name: Shiv Temple
town_description: Nartiang is a historic village in West Jaintia Hills district, about 60-65 km east of Shillong on the Shillong-Jowai road. Once the summer capital of the Jaintia Kingdom, it is famous as the 'Garden of Monoliths' - scattered clusters of ancient Khasi-Jaintia menhirs and dolmens - and for the Nartiang Durga Temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Nearby attractions include Thadlaskein Lake and the district town of Jowai (~25 km).

travel.airport: Nearest airport with scheduled commercial flights: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 170-200 km by road; verify). Shillong (Umroi) airport is closer (approx. 85-95 km; verify) but has limited scheduled services (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 165-190 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus via Shillong/Jowai.
travel.road: Nartiang is approx. 60-65 km east of Shillong on the Shillong-Jowai road (NH-6) and approx. 25 km from Jowai (verify); the Shiv temple is within walking distance of the Durga temple in the village. Reachable by taxi, shared sumo, and state buses from Shillong and Jowai.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivaratri (February-March) is the major festival time (verify crowd claims).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify - one traveller account mentions the temple being opened at an odd hour by the priest's son, suggesting it is not open all day).
